nodes.label: Python Engine Pinned Dependency Lock
nodes.rationale: Fully pinned superset of requirements.txt (adds the uvicorn ASGI server pin) so the container build is byte-reproducible, which the determinism requirements depend on.

nodes.label: Determinism Requirement
nodes.rationale: Identical inputs and configuration must reproduce identical topology/scoring output (e.g. sorted edge selection), otherwise an audited design could not be re-derived later.

nodes.label: Deterministic Seed 42
nodes.rationale: All corpus fixtures are generated with a fixed seed so ML training datasets can be regenerated identically and diffed; reproducibility is the point, not statistical realism.

nodes.label: SYN-4 High-Resistance Cable Variant
nodes.rationale: SYN-4 deliberately uses a high-resistance cable so the corpus contains both successful and failed electrical evaluations — a training corpus of only feasible candidates would teach the ranker nothing about rejection.

nodes.label: Radix-Based UI Primitives
nodes.rationale: Button, Card, Dialog, Select, Slider and Switch are the only styled primitives every feature component imports, so visual drift has a single choke point.

nodes.label: Vite /api Dev Proxy
nodes.rationale: Proxies /api to the Spring Boot backend on port 8080 in development, mirroring what nginx.conf does in production so the client code needs no environment branching.

nodes.label: web-map-next Application
nodes.rationale: Vite + React 18 + TypeScript app scaffolded alongside web-map: server state through TanStack Query hooks over a typed API client, small client-only UI state in two Zustand stores, Leaflet kept vanilla, UI from six Radix-based primitives styled with Tailwind bound to the CSS-variable tokens.

nodes.label: CSS Custom Property Design Tokens
nodes.rationale: Both dark and light palettes are expressed as custom properties so a theme toggle can be added later without rework, even though dark ships as the only theme in this pass.

nodes.label: Three-Tier System Architecture
nodes.rationale: The split keeps authentication, transactions and project ownership in Java, and scientific types/solvers in Python — neither runtime has to grow the other's competency.

nodes.label: Five Evaluation Axes
nodes.rationale: Optimisation quality, engineering feasibility, explainability, scalability and integrated usability — the MVP must provide measurable evidence on all five while marking structural design, foundations, statutory approval and production-scale optimisation as post-MVP.

nodes.label: Golden Demonstration Dataset
nodes.rationale: A small controlled dataset (8-12 WTGs, exclusions, crossings, DEM) is the acceptance basis: the system must produce at least two feeders, avoid hard exclusions, show different winners across the four scenarios, and reject at least one electrically invalid candidate.

nodes.label: CandidateMetrics Optional Attribute Access
nodes.rationale: voltage_margin_pu is read off CandidateMetrics | None without narrowing, meaning scoring tests assume metrics always exist while the model allows a failed/absent evaluation.

nodes.label: FeederTopology mst_edges Type Mismatch
nodes.rationale: Tests pass tuple[tuple[str, ...]] where FeederTopology declares tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] — the edge pair arity is enforced by the type but not by the fixtures.

nodes.label: ScenarioParameters Enum Argument Mismatch
nodes.rationale: grouping_objective and topology_weight_profile are passed as raw str where GroupingObjective / TopologyWeightProfile enums are declared.

nodes.label: Mypy Type-Check Report
nodes.rationale: Captured strict-mode mypy run; the overwhelming majority of findings are in tests/, indicating production modules are typed while the test suite lags the CI type gate.

nodes.label: Manual QA Only Verification
nodes.rationale: This is a UI/architecture migration of existing behavior, not new business logic, and the current app has no test suite to extend — so parity is checked by hand, side by side, with CSV/PDF compared byte-for-byte where feasible.

nodes.label: Build-Alongside Migration Plan
nodes.rationale: web-map-next is built as a sibling so web-map keeps running and deploying unchanged until cutover, avoiding any partially-broken intermediate state.

nodes.label: Migration Global Constraints
nodes.rationale: Design tokens, type roles and the 52px/50px/300px layout shape come from the approved mockup and must not drift without a design conversation; every code-changing step ends with npm run typecheck passing before commit.

nodes.label: SURGE GIS Optimization Service
nodes.rationale: FastAPI microservice split out so GIS processing, route optimisation, electrical analysis and ML inference live in Python rather than the Java enterprise layer.

nodes.label: Preliminary Topology Indicator
nodes.rationale: Screen 4 needs a visible 'preliminary topology only' marker until terrain-aware A* routing replaces the Euclidean MST, so users do not read straight-edge topology as a routed corridor.

nodes.label: Dark Theme Only This Pass
nodes.rationale: Token structure must support a later light toggle without rework, but no toggle UI is built now — scope control, not a technical limit.

nodes.label: No Backend or Database Changes
nodes.rationale: backend-java, optimisation-python and database are untouched and the same REST/JWT contract holds throughout, so the redesign carries no cross-service risk.

nodes.label: Euclidean MST Limitation
nodes.rationale: MST minimizes straight-line topology length only; it ignores terrain, exclusions, parcels, access, junctions, shared trunks and electrical performance, so it understates real corridor length and cannot enforce hard routing constraints.

nodes.label: Coincident Endpoint Rejection
nodes.rationale: Coincident endpoints are rejected as spatially infeasible because they cannot form a non-degenerate refined route.

nodes.label: Route Refinement
nodes.rationale: Raw A* grid paths are converted into cleaner projected LineStrings by removing duplicate and collinear coordinates; exact endpoints and original/refined length plus traversal-cost measurements are preserved so the refinement stays auditable against the raw path.

nodes.label: Visibility Shortcut Acceptance Rule
nodes.rationale: A shortcut is accepted only when its raster supercover contains no blocked cell AND its integrated cost does not exceed the subpath it replaces — geometric smoothing must never trade correctness (crossing an exclusion) or cost for visual tidiness.

nodes.label: SURGE-PY-006 Per-Feeder Minimum Spanning Tree
nodes.rationale: Grouping decides feeder membership and MST decides connections inside a feeder; edges are normalized and sorted for deterministic output. Straight-line UTM distances mean the MST minimizes preliminary Euclidean length only, with terrain-aware routing deferred.

nodes.label: SURGE-PY-007 Uniform Cost Surface
nodes.rationale: A padded north-up float32 raster filled with base cost 1.0 means routes optimize for distance until real layers are rasterized; positive infinity is reserved for hard exclusions and larger finite values for soft penalties. Known gaps: no padding validation, no bounds enforcement, no allocation cap.

nodes.label: SURGE-PY-009 Route Geometry Refinement
nodes.rationale: Shortcuts compare candidate and replaced-subpath cost with the same continuous integration model used by A*, so refinement can never undo A*'s avoidance of finite high-cost cells; coincident endpoints are rejected (HTTP 422) because they cannot form a non-degenerate engineering route.

nodes.label: spatial_constraints_geojson Request Contract
nodes.rationale: One explicit collection carrying constraint_id, constraint_type, routing_mode, buffer_m, cost_multiplier and source; avoidance_geojson may remain as an additive alias but its blanket hard-block semantics must not be applied to ordinary roads and parcels. Feature ordering must not affect the raster or result.

nodes.label: Zero Algorithm Duplication in the Orchestrator
nodes.norm_label: zero algorithm duplication in the orchestrator
nodes.rationale: The assembly layer only calls group_wtgs, build_feeder_mst, route_collector_topology and refine_routing_result from their existing modules, so algorithm behaviour has a single implementation and cannot drift between orchestrator and module.

nodes.label: Supercover Visibility Check
nodes.rationale: Visibility uses a continuous grid-coordinate supercover that tests every raster cell a candidate segment touches, including both side cells at internal corners and boundaries, so a shortcut cannot slip diagonally through a blocked cell; the higher adjacent finite cost is used conservatively on boundaries.

nodes.label: Unclassifiable Features Never Default to WTG
nodes.norm_label: unclassifiable features never default to wtg
nodes.rationale: The else-to-WTG fallback gave towers a fabricated 3.0 MW capacity that inflated feeder_count in group_wtgs and corrupted build_feeder_mst, so the optimiser output was silently wrong rather than visibly wrong; unmatched features now resolve to UNKNOWN and surface for a human decision.

nodes.label: Hard Exclusion vs Soft Penalty Semantics
nodes.norm_label: hard exclusion vs soft penalty semantics
nodes.rationale: Restricted land and confirmed no-go areas are hard exclusions; roads, HT lines and watercourses are soft buffered crossing penalties because blocking a connected road network can make every route impossible, and parcels are soft because an overhead route necessarily occupies land. Crossings and affected parcels must be disclosed, never hidden.

nodes.label: build_project_result()
nodes.rationale: Combines the authoritative ProjectPNCNetwork with the LoadFlowNetworkResult calculated for that exact network; it generates no topology, routes no cables and runs no load flow, limiting itself to rounding, ordering, violation grouping and bounding-box calculation.

nodes.label: Stable GeoJSON Feature Contract
nodes.rationale: Features appear in a fixed order (substation, WTGs by ID, segments by ID, deduplicated poles) with stable top-level IDs and a bbox, so clients can render one predictable schema; pole summaries are calculated from unique physical structures rather than route-local pole counts.

nodes.label: ProjectOptimizationResult
nodes.rationale: Strict Pydantic models reject unknown fields, freeze assignment and forbid non-finite floats, though nested lists and the raw GeoJSON dict stay mutable - the contract is assignment-frozen rather than deeply immutable.

nodes.label: Deterministic Feeder and Segment ID Scheme
nodes.norm_label: deterministic feeder and segment id scheme
nodes.rationale: Feeder IDs (FDR-{N:03d}) and segment IDs (SEG-{feeder_suffix}-{N:04d}) are generated so that identical inputs always produce identical IDs and ordering, which makes assembly output reproducible and testable (determinism is an explicit test case).

nodes.label: PNC Assembly Fail-Loud Failure Model
nodes.rationale: PNCAssemblyError is raised for orphan WTGs, unrouted topology edges, duplicate assignments and broken connectivity rather than dropping them silently, because a partial network returned as a successful assembly would look credible while being engineering-invalid.

nodes.label: MST Graph as Authoritative Topology
nodes.rationale: The mst_graph on each PNCFeeder is authoritative and topology is never reconstructed from geometry; ordered_node_ids is only a deterministic BFS convenience, so geometric coincidence can never silently redefine electrical connectivity.

nodes.label: Fail on Reconciliation Errors
nodes.rationale: Silently joining partial electrical data to the wrong physical asset would produce a credible-looking but unsafe engineering result, so duplicate or unknown identifiers, mismatched associations and non-finite values raise PresentationDataMismatchError.

nodes.label: Keep Presentation Separate from Computation
nodes.rationale: Rounding and JSON naming cannot affect the engineering models used for validation; nullable telemetry keys let clients render one stable schema without probing whether properties exist.

nodes.label: Topology-Only Output After Solver Failure
nodes.rationale: Non-convergence is a valid analytical outcome, not a presentation failure: the physical map, feature IDs and bbox are still returned with null telemetry and an explicit LOAD_FLOW_NOT_CONVERGED violation so users can inspect the proposed network and the map schema stays stable.

nodes.label: PY-034 Land Parcel and Landowner Decision Intelligence
nodes.norm_label: py-034 land parcel and landowner decision intelligence
nodes.rationale: Land policy is burned into the prepared cost surface before scenario generation: UNAVAILABLE parcels become hard exclusions and profiled parcels take an additive owner-interaction and present-value penalty, while layer IDs stay unique so ROW extraction still reports original parcel identity.

nodes.rationale: Conductor selection is computed per segment but has no field in FeederResult and is emitted by no GeoJSON, so a real bill-of-materials line item cannot be filled.

nodes.label: Topology Construction Validation Rules
nodes.rationale: Rejects zero/multiple substations, feeder-count mismatch, duplicate assignments, missing assigned nodes, incomplete coverage and disconnected results — structural invalidity is caught before any downstream cost or electrical work.

nodes.label: Explainability Touchpoint
nodes.rationale: Every screen from 4 onward must answer 'why this result?'; an ML-derived score must never be shown without an experimental label unless the deterministic score is shown alongside it.

nodes.label: Correctness and Safety Requirement
nodes.rationale: Hard engineering constraints (feeder capacity, electrical limits, hard exclusions) must never be silently violated; invalid candidates are rejected outright rather than hidden or downweighted.

nodes.label: Explainability
nodes.rationale: Inputs, constraints, raw metrics, weights, algorithm choice and rejection reasons are all preserved so any result can be audited — designs must be justifiable to regulators, landowners and internal reviewers, which a black-box score cannot do.

nodes.label: ML Ranking Experimental Labeling
nodes.rationale: Deterministic scoring is the baseline and official result; an ML ranker may supplement it only once sufficient labeled data exists and its output is always labeled experimental unless explicitly promoted.

nodes.label: One-Issue-Per-Branch Agent Policy
nodes.rationale: One code-changing agent per branch, never on main/develop, all merges human-reviewed; secrets and private GIS data stay outside AI-assisted prompts and tooling.

nodes.label: KmzGeoJsonConverter
nodes.rationale: The flat Placemark scan is replaced by a depth-first walk keeping folder names on a stack, emitting kmlFolder and kmlFolderPath joined with ' / ' so a bare slash in 220/11KV is not read as a separator; placemarks are deduped on normalised name plus 7-decimal coordinates.

nodes.label: SURGE-PY-021 V1 Constraint Regression Coverage
nodes.rationale: Additive test coverage above the frozen PY-020 boundary: it verifies hard/soft constraint handling, hard-polygon avoidance, byte-identical repeat responses and endpoint rejection without changing the request or response contract.

nodes.label: SURGE-PY-022 Constraint Fixture Provenance Labeling
nodes.rationale: constraint_demo_project_v2.json is labeled a hand-authored Python-contract fixture because it verifies Python behavior after a well-formed payload arrives and does not verify Java's KMZ-to-JSON transformation; the README records what capture evidence is required before calling it a verified KMZ round-trip artifact.

nodes.label: SURGE-PY-024 Pole Placement Integration into the Optimisation Workflow
nodes.norm_label: surge-py-024 pole placement integration into the optimisation workflow
nodes.rationale: Placement runs once, only for the recommended candidate, and pole count is deliberately not a PY-018 scoring objective; a generation error fails the detailed workflow with POLE_PLACEMENT / POLE_NETWORK_GENERATION_FAILED rather than returning a successful result with missing poles.

nodes.label: SURGE Product Vision
nodes.rationale: The product aims to compare complete engineering alternatives rather than merely draw the shortest line between turbines and a substation, combining GIS, electrical analysis, optimization and explainable decision support.

nodes.label: Hard-Violation Candidates Excluded from Normalization
nodes.rationale: Infeasible candidates are kept in the result with raw metrics and rejection reasons but excluded from cohort normalization bounds, so extreme violation quantities cannot compress the scale for feasible candidates.

nodes.label: Deterministic Min-Max Cohort Normalization
nodes.rationale: Scores are relative to the evaluated cohort: adding or removing a candidate changes every normalized score, scores from different jobs or comparison groups are mathematically incomparable, and a single-candidate cohort collapses to 0.0 regardless of weights. The exact NormalizationRange is returned alongside raw metrics so results stay auditable.

nodes.label: AssetClassifier
nodes.rationale: Ordered first-match chain: explicit property, then KML folder evaluated one path segment at a time from the leaf upward, then ID pattern, then UNKNOWN - never WTG. Survey is tested before substation so Anantapur PSS_Borehole resolves as survey.

nodes.label: evacuation_towers Table
nodes.rationale: A dedicated table was chosen because towers have no capacity_mw; wtg_locations' NOT NULL capacity is exactly why they could not be shoehorned in. wtg_locations.status is backfilled APPROVED so existing projects keep working, then defaults to UNKNOWN so new imports must be classified explicitly.

nodes.label: SURGE-JV-006 Ticket
nodes.rationale: Three compounding defects made every KMZ placemark a WTG: the converter discarded folder names and never emitted assetType, the importer used a binary substation test with an else-to-WTG fallback, and the schema had nowhere to put a tower.

nodes.label: Preview-Then-Commit Import Flow
nodes.rationale: Preview classifies and stages without persisting anything and returns the matched rule and evidence per feature; staged imports are held 30 minutes keyed by importId and pinned to the project so a handle cannot be replayed elsewhere.

nodes.label: WtgStatus and isOptimisable()
nodes.rationale: Turbine status lives only in the folder name in the reference file; APPROVED, REGISTRATION and PROPOSED feed the optimiser while CANCELLED, LOW_AEP, TO_BE_SHIFTED and UNKNOWN do not, so only 38 of 99 turbine locations are eligible.

nodes.label: Optimiser Isolation of Non-Optimisable Assets
nodes.rationale: OptimizationJobService filters on status.isOptimisable() before building the Python payload and fails with a distinct message when no turbine is eligible; towers are structurally excluded because they no longer live in the table that service reads.

nodes.label: Shared Classification Rules in Browser and Backend
nodes.norm_label: shared classification rules in browser and backend
nodes.rationale: src/classify.js re-implements the same ordered rule chain in the browser so drag-and-drop rendering and server persistence cannot disagree; verification asserts browser rules agree with backend rules exactly.

nodes.label: Two-Day Demo Productisation Sprint
nodes.rationale: The sprint turns the completed engine into credible product proof without expanding engineering scope; the demonstration must be narrowed before it is allowed to display synthetic, placeholder or unsupported results.

nodes.label: Cross-Cutting Accessibility Gaps
nodes.rationale: Missing ARIA roles and labels, absent focus-visible styling, sub-44px touch targets, colour-only state encoding and feeder colours indistinguishable under deuteranopia/protanopia recur across nav, auth, layers, admin and map.

nodes.label: C-02 No URL Routing
nodes.rationale: View state lives in Zustand with no routes, so nothing is bookmarkable or shareable, back/forward do nothing, and a refresh loses the active view, project and context - which compounds C-10's lack of persistence.

nodes.label: Phase 1 - Trust and Reliability Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Letting API errors propagate is sequenced first because it unlocks all other error UX; the rest of Phase 1 targets confusion, data loss and trust erosion before any feature work.

nodes.label: C-05 Silent API Error Fallbacks
nodes.rationale: Called the most structurally damaging UX issue in the codebase: API modules catch errors and return emptyGeoJson or all-zero BOM values, so TanStack Query treats every map query as successful, isError never fires, a network failure looks like an empty project, and a BOM failure renders a $0.00 bill of materials.

nodes.label: C-11 Toast System Failures
nodes.rationale: Single-toast store, WCAG contrast failures (1.6:1 success, 3.1:1 error), no dismiss, no role=alert or aria-live, no pause on hover, and misleading green styling for 'Imported nothing' - making it unusable as the foundation for all other feedback.

nodes.rationale: Static file-by-file analysis of web-map-next/src identifying 100+ issues across session management, error handling, accessibility, navigation and data visualization; based on source reading only, so a usability test would be needed to validate priorities.

nodes.label: No False-Success in the Demo Path
nodes.norm_label: no false-success in the demo path
nodes.rationale: An optimiser, persistence or refresh failure must be visible to the user, and synthetic scenario-comparison or parcel-impact values must not be presented as calculated results; every visible engineering value must have a real source.

nodes.label: Screen 6 — Reports
nodes.rationale: Exports must carry the same preliminary/planned labeling as the screens they derive from so downstream land and regulatory consumers never mistake MVP output for final engineering data.

nodes.label: Typed API Client (lib/api)
nodes.rationale: A behavior-preserving port of web-map/src/api.js split into typed modules by resource with unchanged method signatures, so Query hooks can call api.method(...) exactly as the old app.js did; per-resource fallbacks (empty GeoJSON, empty arrays, synthetic project) are preserved deliberately.

nodes.label: Demo-Data Fallback Behavior
nodes.rationale: Demo fallbacks on failed API calls are acceptable for early development but must be visibly labeled before any user-facing release, so a failure is never read as a result.

nodes.label: Transparency of Maturity
nodes.rationale: Capabilities must be labeled Implemented, Partial, or Planned at any point in time so users can tell real engineering output from scaffolding.

nodes.label: surge_jwt_token localStorage Key
